newsitem.title: USA: USDA says to work with Congress on farmer loans.
newsitem.headline: USDA says to work with Congress on farmer loans.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Wednesday he was not in a position to endorse Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle's proposal to remove the cap on loan rates and to give USDA authority to extend the life of crop loans.

"We're going to work with Senator Daschle," Glickman told reporters after a USDA meeting. "I'm not in a position to endorse his bill right now other than I do believe farmers need more tools with respect to the marketing of their crops in light of the increased volatility of the markets."
Glickman said he could not comment on the South Dakota Democrat's proposal until he knew how much it would cost.
Glickman has expressed interest in longer loan repayments as a way to bolster farm income.

Asked if the department's budget proposal would be a reiteration of Daschle's proposal, Glickman said: "I think it will be a variety of things, both in terms of commodity programs, as well as credit, as well as technical assistance."

Earlier, Senate Agriculture Committee chairman Richard Lugar said there was no sentiment to alter the crop loan rules written into the "Freedom to Farm" law, throwing cold water on the Democratic proposal.
